body:
Claim: PM loop — maintainer direct-dispatch channel (2026-08-10 standing authorization).
Provenance: maintainer, 2026-09-04, live chat with this session, verbatim 「你认为合理必要的问题都应该处理」, given after this seat surfaced that the `organization_membership_ended` guard is key-gated and the session path was never measured.
Session: `6679d191-11f4-465b-b322-0e0409d76793`
Branch: `claude/issue-15396-session-active-org-measurement`
Worktree: ⚠️ the rig has to be a **cloud** one (the wall needs `org-scoping`, whose only registrar is cloud-private `packages/organizations`), so the working checkout is `objectstack-ai/cloud` at **sibling level** — ⛔ not under `.claude/worktrees`; cloud resolves dependencies by relative path.
Domain: `domain:services` (the guard lives in `packages/core/src/security`); provisional under the direct-dispatch channel, triage may correct.
File surface: **none** — measurement only. Throwaway probes are permitted and ⛔ nothing is committed or pushed.
Container & model: M, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — a security reading whose wrong answer would either declare a live hole absent or invent one.
Clause-②: no — nothing lands.
Serial constraints cleared: no open PR touches `resolve-authz-context.ts` (PR #15365 merged 2026-09-04 as `a72704375`). ⚠️ **cloud#1987 is in flight in the cloud repo** (the framework pin bump) and will move `.objectstack-sha` under this rig — read the pin at the start of the run, record it, and if it moves mid-run say so rather than blending two trees.

os-dev-report

## Outcome: NOT VETTED

**Nothing re-vets `activeOrganizationId` after a membership ends.** A session cookie whose
`activeOrganizationId` points at an organization the user has left reads that organization's
rows and writes into it, on a live `isolated` boot with the real cloud-private
`Organizations` plugin mounted. This is #15256's defect on a session instead of an API key,
and the credential is far more common.

Measured on **both** removal paths, not one:

| after the membership ended | GET | POST | the row, read back from the sqlite file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direct `sys_member` DELETE | **200, total 3** | **201** | `organization_id: org_alpha, created_by: u_exmember_probe` |
| better-auth's own `/organization/remove-member` | **200, total 4** | **201** | `organization_id: org_alpha, created_by: u_victim_probe` |

The second row is the one that closes the card's open question: better-auth's **own** removal
endpoint, driven by the organization's owner, returned 200 and really deleted the row — and
the victim's session came out of it still stamped `org_alpha`, still `revoked_at: null`, still
served. The "better-auth maintains the claim at its source" hypothesis is measured false.

## Rig

Sibling-level cloud worktree, container layout so `link:../../../objectstack/...` resolves.
Pin read at the start of the run and re-read at the end — **it did not move**; cloud#1987 had
already landed before this run began:

```
$ cd .../cloud && git rev-parse --short origin/main && git show origin/main:.objectstack-sha
51a49d9f
8a96e666bfe6f85e635db82007523410fb666d11
```

Real `objectstack serve` of `apps/objectos-ee`, licensed, `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`,
`OS_DATABASE_URL` on a FILE. Boot banner (no stand-in — the real `Organizations` plugin,
never `SimulatedOrgScopingPlugin`):

```
  Driver:  SqlDriver(better-sqlite3)  -> file:.../probe-data/probe.db
  Tenancy: isolated
  Plugins: 44 loaded
           ObjectQL, SqlDriver, HonoServer, PlatformObjects, Auth, @objectstack/setup,
           @objectstack/account, Organizations, Security, Audit, ...
```

Seed: `org_alpha` and `org_beta`, five principals, four `sys_business_unit` rows (two per
organization). RBAC opened **symmetrically** — one permission set on `sys_business_unit`
with `organization_id NULL`, held identically by all five principals — so RBAC is not what
separates any two of them. `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` left at its default `0`, so no
cached envelope is in play.

## Step 1 — the session's organization, confirmed from the session RECORD

Not from a UI: read straight out of the sqlite file, server running.

```
$ sqlite3 -json probe.db "SELECT u.email, s.active_organization_id, s.revoked_at FROM sys_session s JOIN sys_user u ON u.id=s.user_id"
{"email":"betauser@probe.test","active_organization_id":"org_beta","revoked_at":null}
{"email":"exmember@probe.test","active_organization_id":"org_alpha","revoked_at":null}
{"email":"member@probe.test","active_organization_id":"org_alpha","revoked_at":null}
{"email":"owner@probe.test","active_organization_id":"org_alpha","revoked_at":null}
{"email":"victim@probe.test","active_organization_id":"org_alpha","revoked_at":null}
```

## Steps 2 and 3 — remove the membership, keep the session, drive GET and POST

No sign-out anywhere. Path E1, the card's step 2 verbatim:

```
sys_member for ex, before: [{"id":"mem_a_ex","organization_id":"org_alpha"}]
sys_member for ex, after : []
session record for ex, after the delete: [{"email":"exmember@probe.test","active_organization_id":"org_alpha","revoked_at":null}]

get-session [EX-MEMBER, sys_member DELETED] -> 200 positions=["user"] activeOrganizationId="org_alpha"
GET  [EX-MEMBER, sys_member deleted, SAME cookie] -> 200 total=3 rows=[bu_alpha_1@org_alpha bu_alpha_2@org_alpha lEIwZo0ZsFDC8dre@org_alpha]
POST [EX-MEMBER, sys_member deleted, SAME cookie] -> 201 id=ebscqQSvEM4hcfxI
```

Path E2, better-auth's own endpoint, driven by the org owner's session:

```
POST /api/v1/auth/organization/remove-member -> 200 {"member":{"organizationId":"org_alpha","userId":"u_victim_probe","role":"member","id":"mem_a_victim", ...}}
sys_member for victim, after: []
victim's session record: [{"email":"victim@probe.test","active_organization_id":"org_alpha","revoked_at":null}]

get-session [VICTIM removed by better-auth] -> 200 positions=["user"] activeOrganizationId="org_alpha"
GET  [VICTIM, SAME cookie] -> 200 total=4 rows=[bu_alpha_1@org_alpha bu_alpha_2@org_alpha ebscqQSvEM4hcfxI@org_alpha lEIwZo0ZsFDC8dre@org_alpha]
POST [VICTIM, SAME cookie] -> 201 id=nQTkBouV2IR7wgbx
```

Server stopped, both writes read straight back out of the store:

```
$ sqlite3 -json probe.db "SELECT id,name,organization_id,created_by FROM sys_business_unit ORDER BY created_at,id"
{"id":"ebscqQSvEM4hcfxI","name":"exmember-write-after-removal","organization_id":"org_alpha","created_by":"u_exmember_probe"}
{"id":"nQTkBouV2IR7wgbx","name":"victim-write-after-removal","organization_id":"org_alpha","created_by":"u_victim_probe"}
```

### The sharpest line in the run

`positions` is derived from the **same** `sys_member` read that builds `accessible_org_ids`.
Within one run, same principal, same cookie, before and after:

```
get-session [ex-member-TO-BE, membership INTACT] -> 200 positions=["user","org_member"] activeOrganizationId="org_alpha"
get-session [EX-MEMBER, sys_member DELETED]      -> 200 positions=["user"]               activeOrganizationId="org_alpha"
```

`org_member` is gone on the very request that is then served `org_alpha`'s rows. The resolver
**had** the fact that the membership ended, on that request, in hand — and did not act on it,
because the only code that would act on it is gated on an API key. This is not a staleness or
caching problem, and a repair does not need a new read.

## Controls — all four directions held, or this would have measured nothing

```
D  ex-member-to-be   GET   200 total=2   (rows: bu_alpha_1@org_alpha bu_alpha_2@org_alpha)
D  victim-to-be      GET   200 total=2
D  member (control)  GET   200 total=2   -> after both removals: 200 total=5, POST 201
D  beta   (control)  GET   200 total=2   (rows: bu_beta_1@org_beta bu_beta_2@org_beta) -- never an alpha row, before or after
D  signed out        GET   401 UNAUTHENTICATED   -> after: still 401
D  bogus cookie      GET   401 UNAUTHENTICATED
```

- A session with intact membership reads and writes throughout, so the rig serves somebody.
- Signed-out and bogus-cookie are refused throughout, so it does not serve everybody.
- The `org_beta` member is served exactly `bu_beta_1` and `bu_beta_2` and never one alpha row,
  before or after — so the wall genuinely works for a principal whose stored claim matches a
  membership they still hold. What fails is specifically the ended-membership case.
- Every sign-in returned 200. An earlier run lost two principals to better-auth's per-IP
  sign-in limit (3 per 10s) and their controls were vacuous; the probe now retries a 429 and
  refuses to run at all with a missing principal, and the reading above is from the run where
  all five signed in.

## Step 5 — which layer re-vets. Answer: none. Named.

**`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` — `resolveAuthzContext`.** At pin
`8a96e666`, line 294 takes the claim and line 341 gates the only check on an API key:

```
294:      tenantId = tenantId ?? sessionData?.session?.activeOrganizationId;
341:  if (keyPrincipal?.tenantId && input.tenancyPosture) {
343:    if (postureEnforcesWall(posture) && !grants.accessible_org_ids.includes(keyPrincipal.tenantId)) {
351:          reason: 'organization_membership_ended',
```

Line 343 is the **only** comparison of a tenant claim against `accessible_org_ids` anywhere in
the framework:

```
$ grep -rn 'accessible_org_ids' packages --include='*.ts' | grep -v /dist/ | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep 'includes\|indexOf\|has('
packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:343:    if (postureEnforcesWall(posture) && !grants.accessible_org_ids.includes(keyPrincipal.tenantId)) {
```

**better-auth 1.7.2 organization plugin — does NOT maintain the claim.** One writer,
`adapter.setActiveOrganization` (`dist/plugins/organization/adapter.mjs:397`, which calls
`updateSession(sessionToken, ...)`). Every call site passes `session.session.token`, i.e. the
**acting** session only:

```
crud-members.mjs:223  if (session.user.id === toBeRemovedMember.userId && session.session.activeOrganizationId === toBeRemovedMember.organizationId) await adapter.setActiveOrganization(session.session.token, null, ctx);
crud-members.mjs:434  if (session.session.activeOrganizationId === ctx.body.organizationId) await adapter.setActiveOrganization(session.session.token, null, ctx);
```

Line 223 is `removeMember`: it clears only when the caller is removing **themselves**, and even
then only on the one session token making the call. An admin removing someone else clears
nothing, and a second live session of a self-removing user keeps its stamp. Line 434 is
`leaveOrganization`, same single-token shape. Outside `plugins/organization`, no better-auth
code reads `activeOrganizationId` at all — there is no session-read-time validation to fall
back on. This is the code half of what E2 measured behaviourally.

**Framework stamping is CREATE-time only:** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`,
`defaultActiveOrg`, composed into `databaseHooks.session.create.before` (ADR-0093 D9). It sets
the claim at login and never revisits it.

**`packages/organizations` (cloud-private) adds nothing:** its only membership code is a BOOT
gate (`membership-policy-gate.ts`, `assertWalledMembershipPolicyDeclared`), not a request-time
check.

```
$ grep -rn 'activeOrganizationId|getSession|resolveAuthzContext|sys_session' packages/organizations/src/*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'
(no matches)
```

So the chain is: better-auth stamps at login and clears only the actor's own token;
plugin-auth stamps at create; the resolver takes the stamp unvetted for sessions; the
enterprise plugin adds nothing. **Nothing anywhere re-vets it.**

## Step 4 — the kernel-bound wiring: still UNMEASURED, and why

Same wall cloud#1982 hit, re-confirmed at this pin. `kernel-manager` has exactly one registrar,
`packages/objectos-runtime/src/objectos-stack.ts:451`, reachable only through
`createObjectOSStack`, which `apps/objectos-ee/objectstack.config.ts:1466` enters only in its
`else if (cloudUrl)` branch, and `cloudUrl` is set only under `OS_MULTI_TENANT`. Booted:

```
$ OS_MULTI_TENANT=1 ... objectstack serve
MULTI-TENANT arm outcome = exited:1 code = 1
  x [driver-memory] Refusing to start: this driver has NO row-level tenant isolation.
  Detected: tenancy posture `isolated` - a multi-tenant deployment
```

`createHostEnginePlugins()` (`objectos-stack.ts:196-203`) hardcodes `InMemoryDriver` for the
host kernel and no environment variable redirects it. **No stand-in was substituted.** The
hosted SaaS arm remains unmeasured and must not be assumed safe — the same paragraph
cloud#1982 carried forward, unchanged and still owed.

## Blast radius

- **Credential**: an ordinary browser session cookie. Every human user of a walled deployment
  holds one; API keys are the rare case.
- **Window**: from the moment membership ends until the session record expires or is revoked.
  Default `expiresIn` is 7 days (`auth-manager.ts`), and the measured sessions carried
  `expires_at` 7 days out. Nothing in either removal path shortens it — `revoked_at` stayed
  `null` on both.
- **Reach**: read AND write, on a plain org-stamped object, with the write landing stamped
  with the left organization and attributed to the ex-member.
- **Postures**: the walled ones (`isolated`, and by construction `group`), i.e. every walled
  deployment, cloud included.
- **Everyday trigger**: an admin removing a member through the normal product path (E2) is
  enough. No direct database access and no unusual deployment shape is required.
- **Not closed by #15365**: that PR made the posture available and fixed the REST door for API
  keys. The guard it feeds is still `keyPrincipal`-gated, and this run drove sessions only.

## Discipline

Measurement only. Nothing committed, nothing pushed, no PR, no branch. The probe rig was a
throwaway sibling worktree of cloud, verified clean (`git status --porcelain` empty, no diff
against `origin/main`) and then torn down with `git worktree remove` without `--force`. The
probe scripts live outside every repository and are in no tree.

**Measurement delivered — closing.** The reading is comment 5541998221; no code landed, as this card's scope required.

**Outcome: NOT VETTED**, and the hypothesis that would have made it a non-defect was falsified behaviourally, not just by reading code — better-auth's own `/organization/remove-member`, driven by the org owner, returned 200 and really deleted the row, and the removed user's session went on reading and writing that organization.

⇒ Filed as **#15409**, `p0 · security · needs-user-decision`, with the fork (A refuse / B drop the unbacked claim / C revoke sessions) and the four-facet analysis. The repair is a re-ruling of the same question #15256 answered for API keys, so it is the maintainer's, ⛔ not a dispatch this seat makes.

**Verified by this seat after the report, on today's framework `origin/main` rather than the rig's pin**: the framework's only tenant-claim-vs-membership comparison is still the single `keyPrincipal`-gated line in `resolve-authz-context.ts` (one hit across all non-test, non-dist sources, against 59 files that merely mention `accessible_org_ids`). So PR #15365 does not change this reading, and the finding holds on the fixed tree.

**Carried into #15409 rather than lost here**: the four controls; the `positions ["user","org_member"] → ["user"]` transition observed on the very request that was still served; the better-auth analysis (`removeMember` requires `session.user.id === toBeRemovedMember.userId`, so an admin removing someone else clears nothing); and the honest gap — the `kernel`-bound wiring still refuses to boot (`[driver-memory] Refusing to start … posture isolated`), so it is **unknown, not safe**, exactly as cloud#1982 left it.

⭐ Worth recording for the next measuring seat: an earlier run of this probe lost two principals to better-auth's per-IP sign-in cap, which made two controls pass **vacuously**. The dev caught it, made the probe abort rather than run short, and reported only the complete run. A control that cannot fail is not a control.

`pm:dispatched` stripped in the same stroke as the close; `security`, `domain:services`, `priority:p1` retained.
